svg.text: Limit cycles are isolated zeros of the return-map displacement
Example from the quintic Liénard companion (Section 7): ẋ = y − εf(x), ẏ = −x, f(x) = 4x − (20/3)x³ + (8/5)x⁵, ε = 0.04
grey: nearby orbits; they spiral away
from the dashed cycle and onto the
green dots: one orbit hitting the section on successive turns
d > 0: the orbit comes back higher
s = starting height on the section
Π(s) = height at the next return to the section
Zeros of d = closed orbits. Isolated zeros = limit cycles.
Simple zeros (d crosses with nonzero slope) = hyperbolic cycles.
